question: Why did the error rate go up on 07 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: New deployment of catalog v2.23 caused the error rate to spike.
why_chain: The deployment of catalog v2.23 introduced a new version of the RequestHandler that had a NullPointerException.
This NullPointerException led to a high error rate in the service catalog.
The error rate increased from 0.41% to 3.96% in the region us-east.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The error rate spike is due to a sudden increase in request volume.
ruled_out.reason: The request volume for the service catalog in region us-east did not change significantly.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The error rate spike is due to a sudden increase in p95 latency.
ruled_out.reason: The p95 latency for the service catalog in region us-east did not change significantly.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The error rate spike is due to a configuration change.
ruled_out.reason: No configuration change was observed in the evidence.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The error rate spike is due to a dependency issue with an upstream service.
ruled_out.reason: No dependency issues were observed in the evidence.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The error rate spike is due to a data issue.
ruled_out.reason: No data issues were observed in the evidence.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The error rate spike is due to an infrastructure issue.
ruled_out.reason: No infrastructure issues were observed in the evidence.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The error rate spike is due to an unknown issue.
ruled_out.reason: No unknown issues were observed in the evidence.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The error rate spike is not due to a sudden increase in request volume.
ruled_out.reason: It rests on a change that is too early, or in a different service/region, to explain a sudden change here.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The error rate spike is not due to a sudden increase in p95 latency.
ruled_out.reason: It rests on a change that is too early, or in a different service/region, to explain a sudden change here.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service catalog in region us-east rose from 0.41% to 3.96% (+857%), with a change point at 2026-03-07T08:20:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service catalog in region us-east: 1 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.09).
At the same time, request volume for service catalog in region us-east stayed about the same (726 per 5 min before, 891 per 5 min after, +23%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service catalog in region us-east stayed about the same (122 ms before, 121 ms after, -1%).
Deployed catalog v2.23 to us-east (catalog, us-east; 2 min before the change; record R011; fit: right time and place: a strong candidate cause)
High error rate on catalog in us-east (catalog, us-east; 10 min after the change; record R012; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
Deployed catalog v1.24 to us-east (routine release) (catalog, us-east; 198 min before the change; record R010; fit: hours before the change, too early to explain a sudden jump)
catalog: ERROR NullPointerException in RequestHandler.serialize (v2.23) (catalog, us-east; 14 min after the change; record R013; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
catalog: ERROR NullPointerException in RequestHandler.serialize (v2.23) (catalog, us-east; 30 min after the change; record R014; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)

reasons: ✓ A change event (deploys) lines up in time (2 min before the change).
✓ 3 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Roll back the deployment of catalog v2.23 to us-east.
Implement a robust error handling mechanism in the RequestHandler to prevent NullPointerExceptions.
